evidence.quote: Sebastopol once had working railroad trains on Main Street, and the tracks were removed in the late 1980s. Passenger service had ceased in the 1930s, and regular freight service ended in the late 1970s.

evidence.quote: Main Street and Petaluma Avenue were designated one-way streets in the 1980s in an attempt to deal with the town's perennial traffic problem.

evidence.claim: Begin at Highway 1 and follow River Road east through Duncans Mills, Monte Rio and Guernewood Park to Guerneville.

evidence.claim: It takes Front Street through Forestville, then turns south toward Graton and Sebastopol as Gravenstein Highway North.

evidence.claim: Duncans Mills has an original railroad depot and cars, but one building’s old-fashioned appearance belongs to a later revival.
evidence.quote: It has an authentic North Pacific Coast Railroad Depot and several original cars from the old railroad line.

evidence.claim: Alexander Duncan established his sawmill here in 1877, sending lumber to San Francisco.
evidence.quote: In 1877, Alexander Duncan established a sawmill in what is today Duncans Mills. The mills sent lumber to the growing city of San Francisco.

evidence.claim: The narrow-gauge North Pacific Coast Railroad ran through town, then ceased operating in the 1930s.
evidence.quote: Starting in the 1870s, the narrow-gauge North Pacific Coast Railroad ran through Duncans Mills on its way from Cazadero, California, to Sausalito. After being sold several times, the railroad ceased operation in the 1930s.

evidence.claim: A restoration project tied to the 1976 Bicentennial revived buildings and businesses.
evidence.quote: a 1976 restoration project, associated with the celebration of the U.S. Bicentennial, brought about a period of building restoration and business re-vitalization.

evidence.claim: The State Park Sector Office looks like an original town building; it was actually part of that 1976 work.
evidence.quote: A California State Park Sector Office is located in a building constructed to look like an original fixture of the town, but was actually part of the 1976 revitalization.

evidence.claim: but one building’s old-fashioned appearance belongs to a later revival
evidence.quote: A California State Park Sector Office is located in a building constructed to look like an original fixture of the town, but was actually part of the 1976 revitalization.

evidence.claim: Stumptown Days keeps Guerneville’s former English name in its annual parade.
evidence.quote: The annual town parade still commemorates the old place name by calling itself "Stumptown Days."

evidence.claim: Logging in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries gave the place that name; demand for lumber rose after the 1906 earthquake and fires.
evidence.quote: But many of the trees were logged in the late 19th century and the early 20th century, giving rise to the first English name for the place – "Stumptown."  Logging in the area boomed after vast amounts of lumber were needed for rebuilding after the 1906 earthquake and associated fires.

evidence.claim: The name Guerneville honors George Guerne, a Swiss immigrant who owned the town’s sawmill.
evidence.quote: The present name Guerneville was introduced to honor Swiss immigrant George Guerne, a local businessman of the 19th century who owned the town's sawmill.

evidence.claim: Ancient trees survive in the Fife Creek watershed at Armstrong Woods Park, while the surrounding mountain forests include replacement plantings from the logging era.
evidence.quote: A large stand of ancient trees is preserved in the Fife Creek watershed, now the centerpiece of Armstrong Woods Park.

evidence.claim: the surrounding mountain forests include replacement plantings from the logging era
evidence.quote: The extensive redwood forests on the surrounding mountains are less than 200 years old, having been replacement plantings for much of the logging done in the 19th century.

evidence.claim: Sebastopol’s annual Apple Blossom Festival in April and Gravenstein Apple Fair in August continue its connection to an orchard economy.
evidence.quote: The city hosts an annual Apple Blossom Festival in April, Gravenstein Apple Fair in August

evidence.claim: Apples once brought steady prosperity, but competition from other growing regions reduced the industry’s economic importance in the second half of the twentieth century.
evidence.quote: In the second half of the 20th century, the apple industry struggled to compete with other apple-producing regions, and gradually declined in economic significance.

evidence.claim: Vineyards and housing replaced many orchards, and downtown lost its canneries and apple-processing plant.
evidence.quote: The canneries and apple-processing plant are gone from downtown, and vineyards and housing developments have replaced many apple orchards, reducing the demand for freight service.

evidence.claim: One part of the transport network found another use: the former Petaluma and Santa Rosa Railroad passenger depot houses the West County Museum, operated by the Western Sonoma County Historical Society.
evidence.quote: West County Museum, operated by the Western Sonoma County Historical Society in the former Petaluma and Santa Rosa Railroad passenger depot

evidence.claim: Apples once brought steady prosperity
evidence.quote: The apple industry brought a steady rural prosperity to the town.

evidence.claim: Guerneville’s railway connection to the San Francisco Bay ferries arrived in 1877. After train service ended in the late 1930s, vacationers continued coming to its resorts by automobile through the 1950s.
evidence.quote: The San Francisco and North Pacific Railroad in 1877 linked the town to the ferries of San Francisco Bay.  Even with the demise of train service in the late 1930s, the area's resorts remained popular with vacationers who came by automobile through the 1950s.

flags: The Caltrans spreadsheet in 00.txt is a corrupted binary-text capture. The designation is supported by 01.txt, but its date and a route-specific statement of scenic value from the designating body cannot be verified here.
The cache gives route geography but no reliable drive time, grades or curve description. Road-building history is absent; the overview uses the documented Sebastopol street redesign.

Current draft’s lumber-to-vacation narrative is supported specifically for Monte Rio, not as a blanket sequence for every river town; omitted from the overview. Orchard and vineyard scenery is localized to Forestville rather than promised continuously along the road.
